passage: HR note, Wednesday. Sharmila, a junior designer, met me privately. She said a senior colleague from another floor has commented on her clothes and repeatedly asked her out, even after she said no in clear words twice. She had kept a dated list of the messages and the days it happened. She kept asking whether she was overreacting. I told her plainly that it is not her fault and that saying no was enough. I explained that the POSH committee handles such complaints and that she can file a written one; I gave her the form and the committee member's contact details. I did not ask her to confront the colleague herself. She said she would think about it until Friday. I will check in with her then. Minakshi, HR officer

qa.q: Where does the senior colleague work?
qa.a: The senior colleague works on another floor.

qa.q: Why did Sharmila keep asking whether she was overreacting?
qa.a: She seems unsure whether her reaction is justified and may fear she is at fault, which the HR officer answered by saying it is not her fault.

qa.q: What steps helped Sharmila in this meeting?
qa.a: She had kept a dated list of messages, learned how the POSH committee works, and received the form and contact details without being pushed to confront the colleague.

qa.q: What might it mean for Sharmila that Minakshi will check in on Friday?
qa.a: It means Sharmila is not left alone with the decision and can come back with questions.

grounding: A junior faces unwelcome comments and advances; the response is saying no, documenting dates and using the POSH committee.

passage:
It was past 9 p.m., the office in Noida almost empty, the product launch due at midnight, when Bhupen, the senior developer, pulled a chair close to Yash's desk again. "Working late for me, handsome?" His hand settled on Yash's shoulder.
It was the fourth time this month. Yash had laughed it off before, because Bhupen reviewed his code and everyone called Bhupen "a joker".
This time Yash stood up and stepped away. "Bhupen, don't touch me, and stop the comments. I mean it."
Bhupen raised his hands. "Relax, just fun."
"It's not fun for me."
Yash went back to his screen, heart pounding, and opened a note on his phone: the date, the time, the words, and the three earlier times he could remember. At 12:10, after the launch, he emailed HR from home with the note attached.
HR replied at 9 the next morning: "Thank you for reporting this. None of this is on you. We'll meet you at 11, and from today you'll report to a different reviewer."

qa.q: How many times this month had Bhupen done this?
qa.a: It was the fourth time this month.

qa.q: Why had Yash laughed it off before?
qa.a: He felt uncomfortable but afraid to object, since Bhupen reviewed his code and everyone called Bhupen a joker.
He said no clearly, stepped away, wrote down the dates, times and words, and emailed HR with the note that night.
The next morning it thanks Yash, says it is not his fault, sets a meeting at 11 and assigns a different reviewer.

grounding: Shows a colleague's unwanted comments and touch, saying no clearly, documenting dates and words and reporting to HR, with the message that it is not his fault.

passage:
Kiran had kept the note on her phone for three weeks, titled simply "Joseph". 3 March: "You should smile more, it suits you." 10 March: asked twice whether she had a boyfriend, after she said she didn't want to discuss it. 17 March: stood too close behind her chair and said her dress was "distracting".
Joseph was her branch manager in Anna Nagar. Everyone called him "old-fashioned, harmless".
On 18 March, when he started again at the counter, she said clearly, "Sir, please stop commenting on my appearance. It makes me uncomfortable." He laughed and walked away.
That evening after her shift she called Revathi, a senior friend at another branch. Revathi didn't ask what Kiran had been wearing. She said, "That's not your fault. The bank has an Internal Committee. Email them tonight." She stayed on the phone while Kiran typed.
The committee called Kiran the next morning and arranged a meeting that same day.

qa.q: What did Joseph say on 17 March?
qa.a: That her dress was "distracting", while standing too close behind her chair.

qa.q: How might Kiran have felt while keeping the note for three weeks?
qa.a: Uncomfortable and uneasy, unsure whether she would be believed when everyone called him harmless.
She kept a dated note of his words, told him clearly to stop, and with Revathi's support emailed the bank's Internal Committee that evening.

qa.q: How does Revathi respond when Kiran calls?
qa.a: Without blame: she says it is not Kiran's fault, points to the Internal Committee, and stays on the phone while Kiran writes.

grounding: Illustrates a manager's unwanted comments, saying no clearly, documenting dates and words and using the internal committee, knowing it is not her fault.
